result.summary: This PR changes several internal and public validation.cpp/validation.h methods (CheckBlockHeader, CheckBlock, AcceptBlockHeader, ProcessNewBlockHeaders, AcceptBlock, FlushStateToDisk, FatalError, etc.) to return BlockValidationState by value instead of passing it in as an output parameter combined with a separate bool return. It adds MakeInvalid/MakeError factory helpers to BlockValidationState to simplify construction, and updates all call sites in validation.cpp, kernel/bitcoinkernel.cpp, net_processing.cpp, rpc/mining.cpp, blockstorage.cpp, and various tests/benchmarks/fuzz targets accordingly. The stated goal is a no-behavior-change refactor, with one identified minor behavior fix split off into the already-merged #35621.
result.problem: Bitcoin Core's validation code has historically used an output-parameter + bool-return convention for BlockValidationState, which the author found can silently diverge (bool true while state carries stale/invalid info) and is ambiguous about whether an incoming state is consumed across chained calls. This affects anyone maintaining or reasoning about the sensitive block-acceptance path in validation.cpp, and previously surfaced a real inconsistency in AcceptBlock's FlushStateToDisk call that was split into its own fix (#35621).

open_concerns: hodlinator questions whether asserting 'this path never returns Error' via runtime Assume/assert is safe long-term versus using narrower return types; author explained rationale for keeping asserts but agrees narrower types would be superior if easy to achieve.
arejula27 initially argued the refactor should go further and adopt util::Expected instead of a bare BlockValidationState return value; resolved by agreeing to disagree, not a blocker.
Overlap with a separately opened RFC (#35646) proposing a related but different refactor using util::Expected; author supports both and says this PR will be updated if #35646 merges first.
resolved_concerns: arejula27 found a real inconsistency where FlushStateToDisk's returned state was discarded in AcceptBlock; author split this behavior fix into #35621, which merged and is now the base for this PR.
w0xlt found a bug in the block fuzz target where an errant .Error() call made a branch unreachable; author fixed it promptly.
Multiple nits (const-ness, [[nodiscard]], variable naming, brace style, factory method naming) raised by arejula27 and hodlinator have been applied via force-pushes.

categories.rationale: The author explicitly found and documented a real hazard during this refactor ('one instance was identified where the invariant return_value == state.IsValid() was not guaranteed'), which was split off and fixed in the now-merged #35621; the remaining refactor durably removes a class of divergence bugs in the sensitive block-acceptance path and is described by multiple reviewers (arejula27, purpleKarrot, stringintech) as a needed step toward further error-handling work (#35646, #29700), giving it real leverage on future validation-code safety even though it is a no-behavior-change cleanup rather than a fix for an active bug.

uncertainties: Whether the assert/Assume-based 'never returns Error' invariants added late in the PR (per hodlinator's concern) could later be tripped by an unrelated change is unresolved; I treated this as a nonblocking design disagreement rather than a correctness defect.
Relationship to the competing RFC #35646 is fluid; the author says this PR may be updated or superseded depending on which lands first, which could change its priority.

I judged rpc/mining.cpp, net_processing.cpp, and blockstorage.cpp edits as purely mechanical call-site updates rather than substantive category changes; a maintainer of those areas might view the net_processing.cpp Assume additions as worth a closer look.
result.card: This PR refactors several core validation.cpp functions (CheckBlockHeader, AcceptBlockHeader, ProcessNewBlockHeaders, AcceptBlock, FlushStateToDisk, CheckBlock) to return BlockValidationState by value instead of via an output parameter plus a separate bool, aiming to eliminate a class of bool/state divergence bugs in the sensitive block-acceptance path. The author found and split off a real behavior bug this way (now merged as #35621), and reviewers broadly gave concept ACKs (w0xlt, purpleKarrot, stringintech, yuvicc, nervana21) with one full reACK (arejula27), though there is a standing, acknowledged disagreement about whether the codebase should instead adopt util::Expected-typed returns (an alternative explored in the competing #35646 RFC the same author also supports). Review found and fixed a genuine fuzz-test bug (an unreachable assertion branch) along the way. The PR is actively maintained with frequent force-pushes through 2026-09-16 addressing nits, and nothing is currently blocking review, though its final shape may depend on how #35646 resolves.
